I think this is one hand a good idea, on another, not really possible.

The way the scoring is setup, there is a gateway that captures HTTP requests on the Arcade actions to create the scorecard. They effectively run this gateway to see what you are doing. If you submit a container you would have to do finicky things with the network traffic.

On the other hand I agree, I am trying to reverse-engineer the container too, so it would be nice to know more / have more freedom.

firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
TLDR: please allow us to pick our own Docker image for a submission

Why:

A good solution for this competition will likely involve the following:
- An LLM inference framework (VLLM, SGLang, TGI etc.)
- Many isolated sandboxes for untrusted code execution
- Potentially test-time training/fine-tuning of models

Managing and installing all of these things from a Jupyter notebook is very annoying. You effectively need to reverse engineer the Kaggle environment. It's quite unlikely that most of the pre-installed dependencies in the container will be used by many competitors (Who needs TensorFlow?)

On top of the engineering for the competitors, forcing people to find a way to install all of their dependencies from this environment will likely cost a lot in compute time: if it takes 5 minutes just to unpack and install a VLLM wheel, and competitors will use H100s, then each minimal test run will use an extra 5 minutes of H100 time. 

If an hour of H100 time costs 2$, and the average team saves a kernel 5 times a day over 4 months, it will cost you an extra 100$ per team in compute time, just run unpack and install VLLM dependencies for each saved notebook version.

The solution is simple: just allow us to submit a Docker image instead of a notebook. Or a Docker image that serves a jupyter notebook, whichever one is easier. That way, we can create the image once, install all the heavy requirements, and just load it without having to reverse engineer anything.
